links.note: Character-traits table for Anand, closing on 'Now clean up this mess before anyone gets home' - the disorder his invention causes at home, which is 28278.
Phrasal-verb gap fill whose answers include 'rigged up' some decorations - 28281 defines rigged up as assembled temporarily rather than built properly.
What prompted Anand to build the burglar alarm - thefts in the neighbourhood. The invention itself, not the mishap it caused.
How Papa became the target of his own son's burglar alarm - the mishap, which the story tells for its comedy.
Invent an ending explaining what happened to Boppa - continuing the comic mystery the narrative sets up.
Cause-and-effect item on Papa firmly saying NO to trying out the time machine - the family's response to the invention at home.
The moral of the story and how Anand's character reflects it - creativity despite mistakes. About the inventor and his inventions.
Values inferred from Anita's character and how she deals with Anand's inventions - the family around the invention, which is 28278.
What the narrator preferred doing instead of helping Anand - finishing a novel. Anita's reluctance about her brother's project.
Anand's groggy answer when told someone was at the door - told for its comedy in the night-time scene.
Sharma Uncle and Dr Mohan coming to check after the incident - part of the comic aftermath in which no intruder can be found.
The time machine humming softly when they entered the room - the absurd calm that makes the scene funny rather than frightening.
The adults concluding the children imagined it - the comic deflation of the whole episode.
The narrator's argument that it was not imagination, since both she and Anand saw the man - the comic stand-off with the adults.
What Anand suggested had happened to the man - the mishap's unexplained ending, which is what the narrative plays for comedy.
Anand pointing to Boppa's green scarf on the floor - the one absurd trace left, the joke of the scene.
How Papa reacted, roaring from the doorstep after his son's water bag dropped on him - the unit's central comic mishap.
The design of the burglar alarm, triggering only when the door opens gently - how the invention was rigged up, so 28278.
What inspired the time machine - the film 'Back to the Future'. The origin of the second invention.
Who the 'ruffianly fellow' was - Boppa the compound sweeper with his cudgel. The comic reveal that the intruder was no burglar.
Boppa's fate as Anand tells it and the dismantling of the machine - the comic non-resolution the story closes on.
How Anand and Anita react when Boppa breaks in - the frightened-children scene told for its comedy.
Assertion-reason on Papa being sopping wet and scowling because the alarm mistook him for a thief - the mishap and why it is funny.
Who narrates the story - Anita, the sister of the inventor. Establishes the family the invention disrupts.
What Anand rigged up at the front doorstep - a burglar alarm. The invention itself.
How Papa felt after the alarm - 'sopping wet and scowling'. The answer is the mood word 28280 defines: scowling means having an angry or frowning expression.
What Anand thinks he is - a scientist. Anita's framing of her brother the inventor.
The film Anand and Anita saw - 'Back to the Future', the trigger for the time machine.
How long the frantic activity for the time machine lasted - a fortnight. The building of the invention at home.
What inspired the time machine and how his room became a chaotic lab - the invention and the disorder it causes.
How the time-machine experiment causes tension in the family and leads to the burglary - the invention's effect on the household.
Why Boppa's disappearance matters to the story's humour and excitement - the question is explicitly about what makes the episode funny.
The mysterious events around the time machine during the burglary - crashes, humming, a scarf and no Boppa: the comic mystery.
What inspired the burglar alarm - a recent string of thefts in the colony. The reason the invention was rigged up.
Anand's fondness for technical words such as 'blueprint' - vocabulary of assembling and making, which is 28281's territory.
Ma's precaution of watching over her oven and mixer - the family guarding the house against the inventor.
Completing the poem's tone and mood by choosing from brackets - gentle and wishful, thoughtful. 28283 is exactly this bracket-choice summary exercise.
Find other fragrant-flowered trees in your locality and name them in both languages - the follow-on from shiuli being found in many parts of the country.
Why the child writes his name and village on the boats - so someone in a strange land finds them. The act of sending the boats down the stream.
Which flowers the child loads into the boats - shiuli. Named in 28284, not a general boat-launching detail.
